item.title: Space communications startup AnySignal expands into undersea market
item.description: AnySignal, Andrenam plan to develop acoustic modems that would allow submerged systems to exchange data with remote operators through surface buoys and satellite networks

item.title: SpaceX could seek more spectrum to feed terrestrial wireless ambitions
item.description: SpaceX’s acquisition of low-band spectrum to improve Starlink Mobile’s indoor coverage could signal an appetite for even more frequencies to take on established terrestrial wireless giants, analysts say.

item.title: Poland’s SpaceForest completes fourth flight of suborbital PERUN rocket
item.description: JOHANNESBURG — Polish rocket builder SpaceForest completed the fourth launch of its suborbital PERUN rocket, calling it the vehicle’s most successful test to date.

item.title: Kapta Space raises $24 million to expand military radar business
item.description: The Seattle startup is developing lower-cost radar payloads for satellites that could help the military track moving targets on the ground

item.title: Russia may turn to nuclear space weapons to counter U.S. missile defenses, report says
item.description: RUSI study warns that Moscow could target proliferated satellite networks supporting U.S. missile defenses

item.title: The rideshare era is ending. Small satellites need anchor customers for small launch, now.
item.description: If your small satellite is supposed to fly in 2029, you probably don’t have a ride yet. And the cheapest seat in the business is no longer taking your booking.

item.title: Planet addresses sovereign demand and sees promise in large Earth models
item.description: In recent weeks, the Earth observation and analytics company Planet Labs has extended roots in Germany by opening a major manufacturing hub in Berlin and announcing a contract to provide data and analytics to civil government agencies through the German Federal Agency for Cartography and Geodesy (BKG).

item.title: Blue Origin expands in Texas as its founder contemplates an IPO
item.description: Blue Origin announced plans to develop a new manufacturing complex in central Texas as the company’s founder says the firm could be a few years away from going public.

item.title: Commercial space station companies consider future without Crew Dragon
item.description: Companies developing commercial space stations have varying opinions on the severity of the problem of how to get astronauts to and from those stations once SpaceX retires Crew Dragon.

item.title: Crew-12 returns to Earth
item.description: A Crew Dragon returned to Earth Oct. 8 after nearly eight months in space, completing the Crew-12 mission to the International Space Station.

item.title: Space Force seeks clearer view of private capital behind emerging technologies
item.description: A $1.49 million award to startup USAX will support development of a platform to analyze technology investments and inform government co-investment decisions.

item.title: Astrolight delivers first space-to-ground laser communication link to client
item.description: WARSAW, Poland — The Lithuanian space startup Astrolight has announced the successful commissioning of a space-to-ground laser communication link. The link company’s ATLAS-1 laser communication terminal aboard ERMIS-3, an 8U cubesat led by the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens as part of the ERMIS mission, connected with HolOGS-1, the optical ground station of Aristotle University of Thessaloniki in Greece.

item.description: SAN FRANCISCO – Fortastra, a Los Angeles startup developing maneuverable spacecraft for on-orbit security, raised $30 million in a Series A investment round announced Oct. 8.

item.title: The U.S. already oversees commercial space. Novelty is not a regulatory gap.
item.description: A voluntary federal pilot could determine whether America’s next generation of commercial-space businesses operates under clear, generally applicable rules or must first obtain discretionary government permission merely because an activity is new. The Office of Space Commerce’s new Space Commerce Certification (SCC) pilot program may help coordinate novel proposals, but it could become the basis for, or evolve into, an informal permission system if policymakers misinterpret Article VI of the Outer Space Treaty as requiring a bespoke authorization and supervision regime whenever a commercial mission is unfamiliar. Article VI requires states to authorize and continuously supervise nongovernmental activities in outer space, but leaves each state to determine the domestic form, intensity and timing of those functions; it neither requires mission-specific approval because an activity is novel nor compels a customized federal supervisory regime for each unfamiliar use of a spacecraft.

item.title: BlackSky claims six-figure contract with international intelligence agency
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO – BlackSky Technology announced a six-figure pilot contract with an international intelligence agency to provide global, on-demand, high-resolution imagery.

item.title: NASA releases Artemis 2 science data
item.description: Six months after Artemis 2 flew around the moon, NASA has released the full science data collected from the flight, “passing the baton” of the mission to the science community.

item.title: York expands Austin presence with new software-development office
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO — York Space Systems is expanding its Austin, Texas, operations with a new office for software developers.

item.title: Study validates feasibility of European heavy-lift reusable rocket
item.description: A European Space Agency study has found it is technically and financially feasible for Europe to pursue development of a heavy-lift reusable rocket.

item.title: Artemis Accords countries offered opportunities to participate in lunar base and space academy
item.description: NASA is offering countries that sign the Artemis Accords an opportunity to participate in the agency’s lunar base plans as well as in a proposed space academy.

item.title: FCC tees up another D2D boost after approving Starlink Mobile upgrade
item.description: The FCC announced plans Oct. 7 to make more wireless spectrum available for direct-to-device services, a day after authorizing SpaceX to deploy 15,000 next-gen D2D satellites for its Starlink Mobile constellation.

item.title: U.S. military GPS upgrades stretching into 2040s
item.description: Government Accountability Office flags long timelines, limited M-code chip supply and fragmented GPS modernization programs

item.title: The new multi-orbit model of sovereignty and resilience
item.description: In June, SpaceX completed the largest IPO in history, reaching a market value high of over $2 trillion. This valuation has established a new financial center of gravity for the industry, with significant consequences and implications.

item.title: Experience and in-house work speeding SLS/Orion preparations for Artemis 3
item.description: NASA is making faster progress preparing the Space Launch System and Orion for Artemis 3 than on prior missions, in part by taking some work in-house.

item.title: Europe’s push to enhance space autonomy
item.description: As attendees to the International Space Summit walked into the Grand Palais in Paris in early September, a sign of Europe’s ambitions in space greeted them.

item.title: Axiom Space working to revise lunar spacesuit for early Artemis missions
item.description: Axiom Space expects to hear from NASA soon on the configuration for a simplified spacesuit the company will develop for the initial Artemis lunar landing missions.

item.title: Nebex and U.N. to work on supporting emerging space programs
item.description: A startup with plans to help connect space industry suppliers with space projects around the world has signed agreements with a United Nations office.

item.title: California turns to Iceye for flood and wildfire observations
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO — California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced plans Oct. 6 to integrate Iceye satellite-derived flood and wildfire observations into the state’s emergency plans for winter weather.

item.title: NorthStar SDA sensor expansion on track despite investor redemptions
item.description: NorthStar Earth and Space remains on track to expand its in-orbit space domain awareness network, CEO Stewart Bain said, despite heavy investor withdrawals from the blank-check company merger that took it public last week.
